title: AWS Design Principles
description: Apply core AWS design principles for scalability, availability, security, and cost optimization.

data.text: AWS provides a set of design principles that help you build robust systems. These principles come from years of experience running one of the largest cloud platforms in the world.

rows: Design for horizontal scaling using auto scaling and load balancing
Deploy across multiple AZs and use health checks
Recover from failures automatically with retries and fallbacks
Apply least privilege, encrypt data, and use IAM roles
Use caching, CDNs, and right-sized resources
Use pay-as-you-go pricing, auto scaling, and reserved instances
Automate deployments, monitor with CloudWatch, and practice IaC
Use APIs, queues, and events to connect components
Assume failures will happen and design for graceful degradation

data.title: Putting Principles Into Practice
items: **Scalability** — use auto scaling groups instead of fixed instance counts
**Availability** — spread resources across at least two AZs
**Security** — never store credentials in code; use IAM roles
**Performance** — cache frequently accessed data in ElastiCache or CloudFront
**Cost** — use Spot Instances for fault-tolerant workloads

data.title: Beginner Advice
data.text: Start with loose coupling. When services communicate through well-defined APIs or events, you can change or replace one without breaking the others.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Design for scale, availability, and security from the start
Loose coupling makes systems easier to maintain and evolve
Assume failures will happen — design for resilience
